name: Cypriot First Division
content:
The Cypriot First Division is the highest professional football league in Cyprus and is organized by the Cyprus Football Association. It was officially established in 1934, following the creation of the CFA, and has since become the top tier of Cypriot football. The league traditionally includes the strongest clubs in the country, such as APOEL, Omonia, and Anorthosis, which have historically dominated the competition.

The league format has changed several times over the years, but in its modern structure it typically features 14 teams. Each team plays home and away matches during the regular season, followed by a split into championship and relegation groups, where clubs compete for the title, European qualification, or to avoid relegation. Points are carried over into the second phase, and the team finishing first in the championship group is crowned national champion.

Cypriot First Division clubs compete for qualification spots in UEFA competitions, including the Champions League and Europa Conference League. The league is known for its competitive balance, with multiple teams capable of winning the title in different eras, although APOEL remains the most successful club historically. Relegation to the Second Division affects the bottom teams each season, while promotion from lower tiers maintains movement and competitiveness within the system.

name: Cypriot Cup
content:
The Cypriot Cup is the main national knockout football competition in Cyprus, organized annually by the Cyprus Football Association. It was first established in the 1934–35 season, the same year the CFA was founded, making it one of the oldest football competitions in the country. It is considered the second most important domestic tournament after the Cypriot First Division.

The competition is open mainly to clubs from the Cypriot First and Second Divisions, with the format being a single-elimination knockout tournament. Over the years, its structure has changed, but the modern version typically includes multiple rounds leading to a final played at a neutral venue, often the GSP Stadium in Nicosia. The winner is awarded the national cup title and also qualifies for UEFA European competitions, most commonly the Europa League or Europa Conference League.

Historically, the Cypriot Cup has been dominated by a few major clubs, with APOEL being the most successful team in the competition’s history. Other traditional winners include Omonia, Anorthosis, AEL Limassol, and Apollon Limassol. The tournament is known for producing surprises and memorable runs from underdog teams, making it an important and highly competitive part of Cypriot football culture.
